title: Priming lag scrapbook: microbench notes and quick artifacts
body:
Purpose: quick, messy running notes on an odd recurring effect I call 'priming lag' — momentary p95/p99 spikes after an otherwise steady QPS when the workload includes many distinct prompt prefixes and variable sequence lengths. Trying to capture reproduction, hypotheses, and commands so I can iterate faster.

Setup summary:
- Cluster: dev-fleet-staging (8x A100s, mixed 80GB/40GB), serving runtime branch: feature/kv-prime-optim (PR linked above).
- Model: redwood-13b-qa-quant (int8-ish), context window 2048, tokenizer ~1.2k avg prompt tokens in these runs.
- Traffic generator: custom wrk-like shim (repo: GH link above). Pattern: steady 60 qps for 10m, insert 30s bursts at 300 qps every 2m to emulate search spikes.
- Experiments: incremental: cold start vs primed cache vs partial-key-hit mix. Also varied batching (max-batch 8->32) and batch-timeout 2ms/8ms.

Key commands (for repro):
- spawn load: ./tools/loadgen --qps 60 --burst 300 --burst-interval 120 --duration 600 --seed 20250914 --prompts prompt-list.json
- curl health + metrics for a node: curl -sS http://node-3:9000/metrics | grep kvcache_hit
- snapshot tail traces: ./bin/trace-collector --filter request.duration>200 --out traces/20250914-1.json

Observed artifacts (raw notes):
- Baseline (primed): 60 qps steady for 10m -> p50 18ms p95 62ms p99 140ms. CPU/gpu util stable. kvcache_hit_rate ~0.82.
- After idle 2m then resume: immediate p95 jump to 300-450ms for 12-18s then back to baseline. kvcache_hit_rate dropped to ~0.32 during spike window and recovered.
- Bursts: when burster hits 300 qps, we see two-phase spike: an early 1-3s window p99 up to 1.2s (queueing) and a secondary 10-20s tail (priming-lag) with p95 ~350ms. Secondary phase correlates with cache churn metrics (eviction_count increased).

Hypotheses:
1) KV cache is granulated by token-prefix hash; burst injects many new prefixes, causing eviction of high-value entries (thrash). Recovery when popular prefixes re-accumulate.
2) Batching heuristics: when many unique short requests arrive, batching collapses and GPU kernel warm paths switch, creating a transient higher per-token overhead.
3) Memory pressure on 40GB nodes causes transient spilling to CPU for some tensors leading to tail latency until optimizer threads re-pin pages.

Quick experiments run and notes:
- Batch-timeout increase to 8ms: reduced initial burst p99 (1.2s -> 800ms) but lengthened tail window (18s -> 35s). Means more aggregation helps immediate saturation but delays recovery?
- Hard pinning kvcache_size + eviction-policy LRU->CLOCK: reduced eviction_count by ~56% during burst, tail window shortened to ~9s and p95 reduced 20%. Promising.
- Disabled secondary prefetcher (feature flag): no visible improvement; maybe prefetcher not related.
- Reduced model concurrency per GPU (2->1): lowered p99 peaks but overall throughput insufficient for production.

Micro-observations from traces:
- Many requests in tail window show an extra 120-280ms in "encode->kv-lookup" stage compared to baseline. Suggests expensive lookup or lock contention.
- Lock stats: mutex wait time increases ~6x during tail. Suspect global shard lock on kvcache resize/evict path.

Next small actions (TODOs):
- Add per-shard kvcache metrics surface (hit/miss/evict/lock-wait) into /metrics for easier correlation. (GH: add metrics PR)
- Try CLOCK->Segmented LRU and re-run single-burst test with trace-level sampling 1% (priority).
- Instrument kernel-selection logs to see if path flip correlates with tail. (low-overhead sampling only)
- Run isolation test on A100-80GB-only pool to rule out 40GB spill hypothesis.

Notes to self / rough conclusions so far:
- "Priming lag" appears to be a composite: partial cache thrash + lock contention while system rebuilds hot-prefix set. Bigger batches reduce immediate saturation but can prolong the rebuild window.
- Short-term mitigation for production: strong kvcache-size reservation for high qps customer pools + conservative eviction policy + small increase in batch-timeout (only for bursts) via adaptive policy.

Open questions:
- Can we do quick adaptive priming: on burst detection temporarily bump cache retention for recently seen prefixes? Complexity: perf vs memory.
- Is there a way to make eviction less lock-heavy (per-shard free-list + background compaction)?

Random log snippets copied here for later search:
- "2025-09-14T13:22:03Z node-3 kvcache: evict 1248 entries (target 1024)
  wait-time-ms=12 locks=3"
- "trace: req=0x7f9 encode->kv 180ms extra (keyset=162)"

If I get time: collect per-prefix access heatmap over a 10m window and try a synthetic 'warm-up' injection that replays top-1k prefixes before burst. That should prove if priming-only solves it.

End of today's messy log. Will iterate after the CLOCK->segmented-LRU pass.

-- mateo
